Jared / Marissa — quick commercial note: we can structure a 12-month committed plan where ArborEdge pays a predictable monthly invoice tied to a committed token bucket. For the onboarding credit, I recommend: 

- Option A: One-time credit equal to 10% of the first 3 months' committed value (applied after invoice),
- Option B: A staged credit where 50% is applied on go-live and 50% after completion of the first 90-day integration sign-off.

I'll model both in the attached spreadsheet and include a sample invoice cadence that maps to Azure private plan entitlements. If procurement needs net-30 vs net-45, call that out and we can route to finance for approval.

Laura, for the SOW redlines: primary asks we've seen from customers — explicit data residency clause, audit rights, and a short SLA paragraph for dedicated capacity. Can you take the attached SOW and mark up changes?

Thanks team — Laura here from Legal. I reviewed the attached SOW and have three proposed redlines to keep the private offer consistent with our marketplace obligations and to protect both parties: 

1) Data residency: we can commit to region-specific residency in a named Azure region and include an attestation appendix. The customer must identify the region in the purchase order.
2) Audit scope: limited to SOC2 + data flow review; audits to be scheduled with 30 days' notice and mutually agreed scope.
3) Liquidated damages: replace open-ended indemnity for capacity outages with a service credit schedule tied to SLA tiers (for Dedicated or Reserved capacity only).

I'll attach a redlined PDF and a clean SOW draft. If ArborEdge needs stronger warranty language, we'll need legal-to-legal conversation.

Laura Bennett | Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
